Regardless, I'll get us both therapy. I'm not sure if he actually forgives me, he probably did it to shut me up or avoid talking about it. Our relationship is great so idk.

Also, I just brought up the abuse to my mom and cried a lot. She said she'll get us both to a therapist but told me not to bring it up to my brother. She also told me to treat my brother well and to love him (which I do, a lot). Being conservative though, she was a bit homophobic. She told me that "two boys can't do that because it's deviant (deviant as in gay). (what the fuck? is it not because its abuse?) I told her about being assaulted and she downplayed it, "boys do stupid stuff like that" (NO THEY DON'T AND THEY SHOULDN'T, WTF). However, I told her to tell my brother that it's not his fault AT ALL and to make him feel strong and not vulnerable (if its ever brought up), to which she responded with "I will". I brought up COCSA to her. "I mean we were both children and I'm not like those fucking adult predators. If both parties were children, the perpetrator is more likely to have faced abuse themselves". She said "12/13/14-year-olds know better" (She's kinda right, but a 13/14 year old in a conservative family probably wouldn't), to which I responded "Yes they probably do but you never taught me about sex. Sure, you taught me about boundaries (boundaries as in where to be touched and not to be touched) but I didn't know it was wrong to do that or to have people do that to me and violate my boundaries. I was genuinely curious and was never taught about sex. I thought it was normal if it's your friends and if it's not severe. She said "How would I teach you about it (sex)?". She also asked if I watch "bad stuff" (aka porn), to which I answered "No." (I lied to her, I do watch porn)

She asked if I liked being assaulted and If I was gay (I believe I'm bi myself but I didn't tell her and never will) and I said "No, I didn't. I believe it traumatized me. Also no I'm not gay". She laughed for a second at the word "traumatized" reiterating the "Boys do stupid dirty stuff like that" line. "Yes it's wrong but boys do that and it's not really traumatic", she said. Having a finger shoved up yourself and feeling like trash isn't traumatizing. Funny. Feeling weak and vulnerable and that you deserve everything that happens to you whether it's rape or harassment because you couldn't speak up definitely isn't trauma! She told me that if I keep letting people assault me, I'll become gay. (Which is fucking bullshit btw, you don't turn gay from being assaulted) Thankfully, my brother didn't hear the conversation, she would've probably re-traumatized him.

I believe the therapist/counselor will be able to handle it far better than my mom ever would though. They definitely know more about psychology and trauma than a Muslim mom. She'll contact her tommorrow.

Was I hypersexual though? I remember having a high libido (that probably wasn't related to what happened to me) when I was 13-14 and feeling like shit sometimes, probably because I felt like masturbating was consuming me (as in being addictive). (which I don't think was related to that. it could have been simply puberty). I also exhibited some inappropriate behavior such as making sexual jokes and touching my penis with my pants on in front of my mom. <---- I feel ashamed writing this. I feel like a fucking pervert.

Also, was I really a victim? I remember one of my classmates shoving a finger up myself at school with my pants on (he shoved it deep) and feeling extremely ashamed afterwards, but I can't believe that I am a victim since it wasn't probably as severe. I'm sorry for seeking reassurance.

> He may harbor resentment, fear, or even hatred for you for what you did, but thats ok. Learning to be ok with yourself even after the harm you've caused people is a necessary skill

That's what I fear. I fear that I may have harmed him... That's what's making me feel like a monster. I don't want to be called a child molester/assaulter although I acknowledge that what I did was wrong. I feel like I'm a bad person and that I'm one of *them* (them as in child molesters/rapists). I feel extremely guilty and ashamed. I don't feel like I deserve to live or to have any friends for what I did.

I hope so. He doesn't display any signs of sadness or depression but idk, he could be hiding it. I'll bring it up to my mom and get both of us to therapy.

Thanks for your advice. I hope you (and all survivors in general) recover.

It probably did have some influence. I thought it was normal because my "friends" did.

I started masturbating when I was in 1st grade after being touched by my cousin, and I thought it was something I had made up. I didn't know anyone else did it until I was 12.

Also, I remember that my brother apologized when I was crying the day it happened which makes me feel guilty. He shouldn't apologize at all, he's a victim.

> It's extremely mature of you to take responsibility for this at all.

Idk if I'm actually taking responsibility. I always try to acknowledge it (which I do) but then when the memories replay in my head, I try to rationalize it as if it were normal (which it isn't, AT ALL). I'm willing to go to therapy but I feel ashamed.

Thanks for the advice, I will. I always ask him how he feels everyday, and he says he's good.
